subject: chemistry

instructions: The paper is divided into two sections. Section A is compulsory. Attempt any four main questions from Section B. Intended marks are given in brackets [ ].

sections.name: Section A
sections.rule: Attempt all questions from this section

questions.question: The atomic number of an element is 13. It belongs to ______
questions.solution: (c) Third period and group 13. Z = 13: 2, 8, 3 - three shells (period 3) and 3 valence electrons (group 13 / IIIA).

questions.question: The alkyl group in ethanal is
questions.solution: (c) Methyl. Ethanal is CH3-CHO; the alkyl group attached to the -CHO group is methyl (CH3-).

questions.question:
Three separate samples of an aqueous solution of compound Q are tested. The results of the tests are shown below.
| Sample | Test | Observation |
| Sample 1 | Add silver nitrate solution | White precipitate, soluble in excess ammonium hydroxide |
| Sample 2 | Add aqueous ammonia | White precipitate, soluble in excess |
| Sample 3 | Add aqueous sodium hydroxide | White precipitate, soluble in excess |
The compound Q is:
questions.solution: (c) Zinc chloride. White ppt with AgNO3 soluble in NH4OH shows chloride (AgCl); a white ppt soluble in excess of both NH4OH and NaOH shows Zn2+. Hence zinc chloride.

questions.topic: Properties of ionic compounds from data
questions.question:
The table shown below gives information about four substances A, B, C and D.
| Substance | Melting point | Conductivity (solid) | Conductivity (liquid/aqueous solution) |
| A | 295 | Good | Good |
| B | 1890 | Poor | Good |
| C | 1290 | Poor | Good |
| D | 1160 | Poor | Poor |
Identify the ionic compounds from the above given substances.
questions.solution: (b) B, C. Ionic compounds have high melting points and do not conduct in the solid state but conduct in molten/aqueous state - B and C. (A conducts as a solid - a metal; D does not conduct at all - covalent/macromolecular.)

questions.question:
The diagram shows apparatus used to electroplate a cup with nickel metal. [An iron cup and a nickel electrode dip into nickel sulphate solution and are connected through an ammeter to a battery.]
The experiment did not work. What change is needed in the experiment to make it work?

options.a: Add iron sulphate solution instead of nickel sulphate.
options.b: Replace the nickel electrode with a graphite electrode.
options.c: Reverse the connections of the battery.
options.d: Increase the temperature of the electrolyte.

questions.solution: (c) Reverse the connections of the battery.. For electroplating, the article (iron cup) must be the cathode (- terminal) and the plating metal (nickel) the anode (+ terminal); the battery connections were the wrong way round.

questions.question: Bromine water is a reddish-brown solution. When bromine water is added, which of the following compounds would get decolourised?
questions.solution: (d) C4H8. C4H8 (butene, CnH2n) is unsaturated and adds bromine, decolourising bromine water; C2H6 and C7H16 are saturated alkanes (C3H9 is not a valid formula).

questions.solution: (b) NH3. Ammonia is basic and reacts with conc. H2SO4: 2NH3 + H2SO4 -> (NH4)2SO4 (white solid).

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.topic: Preparation of insoluble salt from insoluble base
questions.question: Identify the correct method of preparation of lead carbonate from lead hydroxide.

options.d: Decomposition by acids and then precipitation

questions.solution: (c) Neutralisation followed by precipitation. Insoluble Pb(OH)2 is first neutralised with dilute HNO3 to give soluble lead nitrate: Pb(OH)2 + 2HNO3 -> Pb(NO3)2 + 2H2O; then PbCO3 is precipitated: Pb(NO3)2 + Na2CO3 -> PbCO3 + 2NaNO3.

questions.question: Which oxide cannot be reduced by carbon under any industrial temperature?
questions.solution: (c) CaO. Calcium is a highly reactive metal (above carbon in the reactivity series); its oxide is not reduced by carbon - Ca is extracted by electrolysis.

questions.question:
When a compound was electrolysed using inert electrodes, the gas released at the anode rekindles a glowing splinter. The compound that will produce this observation at anode is
P. Dilute sodium chloride solution
Q. Dilute copper sulphate solution
R. Concentrated NaCl solution
S. Pure water
Which is the correct option?
questions.solution: (a) P and Q. Oxygen (rekindles glowing splinter) is liberated at the anode from dilute NaCl (OH- discharged) and dilute CuSO4. Concentrated NaCl gives chlorine; pure water is a non-electrolyte and practically does not conduct.

questions.question: When a salt is treated with sodium hydroxide solution it gives gas X. On passing excess of gas X through reagent Y a brown colour precipitate is formed. X and Y respectively are-
questions.solution: (c) X = NH3 and Y = K2HgI4. Ammonium salts + NaOH give NH3, which gives a brown precipitate with Nessler's reagent (alkaline K2HgI4).

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question:
Two statements are given one labelled Assertion (A) and other labelled Reason (R). Select the correct answer to the questions from the a, b, c and d as given below.
Assertion: Strength of the acid or base decreases with dilution.
Reason: Ionisation of an acid or a base increase with dilution.

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of the assertion
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of the assertion
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: (d) A is false, but R is true.. Strength depends on the degree of ionisation, not on concentration; dilution increases the degree of ionisation, so strength does not decrease (only the concentration decreases). A is false, R is true.

questions.question: Which contain more molecules?
questions.solution: (a) 3g Hydrogen. 3 g H2 = 1.5 mol; 32 g O2, 28 g N2 and 44 g CO2 are each 1 mol. Most moles -> most molecules.

questions.topic: Electrolysis of CuSO4 with platinum electrodes
questions.question:
The diagram shows an electrolysis of copper sulphate using platinum electrodes. [Two platinum electrodes dip into copper sulphate solution; the left electrode is connected to the + terminal of the battery and the right electrode to the - terminal; the labels A and B point to the electrodes - see figure.]
(a) Which is the oxidising electrode A or B and write the reaction taking place at this electrode.
(b) At which electrode will reddish brown metal deposit, A or B?
(c) Will the concentration of copper ions increase, decrease or remain same in the electrolytic solution? Justify your answer.
(d) What happens when platinum electrode is replaced with copper electrodes?
questions.solution:
(Reading the figure: B is the electrode connected to the positive terminal (anode) and A the one connected to the negative terminal (cathode).)
(a) B, the anode, is the oxidising electrode: 4OH- - 4e- -> 2H2O + O2 (oxygen gas evolved).
(b) Reddish brown copper deposits at A, the cathode: Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu.
(c) Decreases - Cu2+ ions are discharged at the cathode, but the inert platinum anode does not dissolve to replace them, so the blue colour of the solution fades.
(d) With copper electrodes, the copper anode dissolves (Cu - 2e- -> Cu2+) instead of oxygen being evolved, and copper is deposited at the cathode; the concentration of Cu2+ (and the blue colour) remains the same - the anode becomes thinner and the cathode thicker (electrorefining).

marking_points.point: Anode (electrode connected to +, B) is the oxidising electrode
Cu2+ concentration decreases: discharged at cathode, not replaced by inert anode
With Cu electrodes the anode dissolves, Cu deposits at cathode, concentration stays same / no O2

questions.figure_desc: Electrolytic cell with two platinum electrodes in copper sulphate solution connected to a battery (+ on left), with labels A and B pointing to the electrodes

questions.question:
Match the Column A with Column B and write answers as (a...1, b...2...)

questions.topic: Mass and gas volume from equation
questions.question:
Find the mass of lead formed by reduction of 344 g of red lead (Pb3O4) in a current of hydrogen and also find the volume of hydrogen used up at STP. [Pb = 208, O = 16, H = 1]
Pb3O4 + 4H2 -> 3Pb + 4H2O
questions.solution:
Molar mass of Pb3O4 = 3(208) + 4(16) = 688 g; moles = 344/688 = 0.5 mol.
Pb formed = 3 x 0.5 = 1.5 mol = 1.5 x 208 = 312 g.
H2 used = 4 x 0.5 = 2 mol = 2 x 22.4 = 44.8 dm3 at STP.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
You are given the following information about four elements P, Q, R and S:
P has the lowest ionisation potential in its period.
Q has atomic no. 13.
R has 7 valence electrons.
S is an alkaline earth metal in period 3.
Use the above information and answer the following: [Do not identify the elements]
(a) Between P and S which one will have a larger atomic radius? Give reason.
(b) Write the formula of the compound formed between Q and R.
(c) State the type of bond formed between P and R.
(d) Arrange P, Q, R in increasing electronegativity.
questions.solution:
P is in group 1 (lowest IP in its period); Q = 2,8,3 (group 13); R is in group 17; S = 2,8,2.
(a) P has the larger atomic radius - P (group 1) lies to the left of S (group 2) in period 3, so it has a smaller nuclear charge pulling the same number of shells.
(b) QR3
(c) Ionic (electrovalent) bond
(d) P < Q < R

marking_points.point: P larger, with reason (smaller nuclear charge / to the left in the period)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Give reasons (coke layer, liquid NH3, storage of HNO3)
questions.question:
Give reason:
(a) Powdered coke is sprinkled on the electrolytic mixture during extraction of aluminium from its ore.
(b) Liquid ammonia is used as refrigerant in ice plants.
(c) Concentrated nitric acid is mostly stored in amber coloured bottle.
questions.solution:
(a) The coke layer reduces heat loss by radiation from the surface of the electrolyte and prevents burning/oxidation of the anode in air.
(b) Liquid ammonia has a high latent heat of vaporisation; on evaporating it absorbs a large amount of heat from the surroundings, causing cooling.
(c) Nitric acid decomposes in sunlight (4HNO3 -> 4NO2 + 2H2O + O2); amber bottles cut off light and prevent this decomposition.

marking_points.point: Reduces heat loss / prevents oxidation of anode
High latent heat of vaporisation; absorbs heat on evaporation
Prevents photodecomposition of HNO3 by light

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: An organic compound is found to possess H = 6.7% and O = 53.3% and remaining is carbon. Its vapour density is 30. Find the molecular formula of the compound? [atomic weight of H = 1, O = 16, C = 12]
questions.solution:
C = 100 - 6.7 - 53.3 = 40%.
C: 40/12 = 3.33; H: 6.7/1 = 6.7; O: 53.3/16 = 3.33
Ratio C : H : O = 1 : 2 : 1 -> empirical formula CH2O (mass 30)
Molecular mass = 2 x VD = 60; n = 60/30 = 2
Molecular formula = C2H4O2

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Rahul sets up an experiment of electroplating spoon with silver. Answer the questions based on the experiment:
(a) Name the electrolyte preferred in this process and why?
(b) Which equation for the reaction at the anode is correct?
1. Ag -> Ag1+ + 1e-
2. Ag + 1e- -> Ag1+
3. Ag1+ - 1e- -> Ag
4. Ag2+ + 2e- -> Ag
(c) What will you observe at anode during the experiment?
questions.solution:
(a) Sodium argentocyanide, Na[Ag(CN)2] (or potassium argentocyanide) - it dissociates slowly, releasing Ag+ ions at a slow, steady rate so the deposit is smooth, uniform, even and long-lasting.
(b) Equation 1: Ag -> Ag+ + e- (oxidation at the anode).
(c) The silver anode gradually dissolves and becomes thinner (loses mass).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Below are the few reactions of compound P; analyse them and answer the following:
A. Compound P --(conc. H2SO4)--> Ethene + H2O
B. Compound P + acetic acid --(conc. H2SO4)--> Z + H2O
(a) Identify P and give a completely balanced equation for the reaction (A).
(b) Give the chemical formula of Z and state the type of reaction involved when P reacts with acetic acid.
(c) What is glacial acetic acid?
questions.solution:
(a) P is ethanol (C2H5OH). C2H5OH --(conc. H2SO4, 170 °C)--> C2H4 + H2O
(b) Z = ethyl ethanoate (ethyl acetate), CH3COOC2H5; the reaction is esterification.
(c) Pure (anhydrous) acetic acid which, on cooling below 16.6 °C (about 17 °C), freezes to an ice-like solid is called glacial acetic acid.

marking_points.point: Pure acetic acid that freezes to ice-like solid at about 16.6 °C

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
[Faded in the scan; the two volumes are illegible.] ___ ml of methane on complete combustion with ___ ml oxygen, assuming water condenses. Calculate the volume of carbon dioxide and any leftover gas, if any.
CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O
questions.solution:
By Gay-Lussac's law, 1 vol CH4 : 2 vol O2 : 1 vol CO2 (water condenses, so its volume is ignored).
If V ml of methane burns completely: O2 used = 2V ml; CO2 formed = V ml; leftover O2 = (O2 supplied - 2V) ml.
For example, 20 ml CH4 with 100 ml O2: O2 used = 40 ml, CO2 formed = 20 ml, unused O2 = 60 ml. (Substitute the printed values; the figures on this copy are not legible.)

marking_points.point: Volume of CO2 = volume of CH4 (1:1)
Leftover O2 = O2 supplied - 2 x volume of CH4

questions.question: Richa finds two unlabelled test tubes in laboratory. She knows that both contain sulphuric acid, one concentrated and the other dilute. Using copper metal, how will she identify the concentrated sulphuric acid? State her observation in both the test tubes.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Explain: MgCl2 high mp; atomic size across a period
concepts: strong electrostatic forces in ionic compounds
questions.question:
Explain why?
(a) Magnesium chloride has high melting point and boiling point.
(b) Atomic size decreases across a period in the periodic table.
questions.solution:
(a) MgCl2 is an ionic compound; its Mg2+ and Cl- ions are held by strong electrostatic forces of attraction in a crystal lattice, so a large amount of energy is needed to break them.
(b) Across a period the number of shells remains the same but the nuclear charge increases, so the electrons are pulled closer to the nucleus and atomic size decreases.

marking_points.point: Strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions
Nuclear charge increases with same number of shells

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Electron dot diagrams: CaO and N2
questions.question:
Draw the electron dot diagram of the following compounds:
(a) Calcium oxide
(b) Nitrogen molecule
questions.solution:
(a) CaO: Ca (2,8,8,2) transfers 2 electrons to O (2,6): shown as [Ca]2+ and [O with 8 electrons (6 dots + 2 crosses)]2-.
(b) N2: each N (2,5) shares three electrons, forming a triple bond - three shared pairs between the N atoms and one lone pair on each N (N≡N).

marking_points.point: CaO: transfer of 2 electrons, Ca2+ and O2- with octet and charges
N2: three shared pairs and one lone pair on each N

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Vapour density, molecular mass and molar volume
questions.question:
Solve:
(a) Calculate the VD and molecular mass of gas X if 200 ml of the gas at s.t.p weighs 0.40 g. [1 litre of H2 at s.t.p weighs 0.09 g] [2]
(b) Calculate the volume at STP occupied by ethane gas (C2H6). (atomic weight of C = 12, H = 1) [1]
questions.solution:
(a) Mass of 200 ml H2 at STP = 0.09 x 0.2 = 0.018 g.
VD = mass of 200 ml of X / mass of 200 ml of H2 = 0.40 / 0.018 = 22.2
Molecular mass = 2 x VD = 44.4 (≈ 44)
(b) Molar mass of C2H6 = 2(12) + 6(1) = 30 g; 1 mole (30 g) of ethane occupies 22.4 dm3 at STP. (No mass is printed in the question; the answer assumes one mole/30 g.)

marking_points.point: 30 g (1 mol) of C2H6 occupies 22.4 dm3

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B

(b) Dilute hydrochloric acid is added to potassium carbonate.

questions.question:
The following questions are related to the extraction of aluminium from its ores.
(a) Name the solution used to react with bauxite ore as a first step in obtaining pure aluminium oxide, give the suitable reason for addition of this solution.

questions.topic: Electron dot structure of hydronium ion
questions.question: Draw the electron dot diagram showing formation of positive ion formed when an acid dissolves in water.
questions.solution: H2O + H+ -> H3O+. Oxygen in water has two shared pairs with two H atoms and two lone pairs; one lone pair is donated to the H+ ion forming a coordinate bond. Show [H3O]+ in square brackets with + charge: O with three bonding pairs (to three H) and one lone pair.

marking_points.point: Water molecule with two lone pairs on O, one donated to H+ (coordinate bond)
Hydronium ion [H3O]+ shown with brackets and + charge
